top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Granfondo Bulgaria. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 87 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Bulgaria's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
74ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
6,433ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Granfondo Bulgaria, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Bulgaria. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 87, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
6,433ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo Bulgaria. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 87 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 87 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.weather: June in Velingrad, Bulgaria — Late June in Velingrad's Rhodope Mountains typically features mild-to-warm mountain weather with temperatures 15-25°C (59-77°F). Expect variable conditions at elevation with possible afternoon showers. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Granfondo Bulgaria. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Granfondo Bulgaria’s 87 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Granfondo Bulgaria. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Granfondo Bulgaria rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 87 miles of mixed terrain in Velingrad, Bulgaria.
